title: Total Retinal Detachment (TRD): Clinical Masterclass
summary: Total Retinal Detachment (TRD) represents an ophthalmic emergency defined by the complete separation of the neurosensory retina from the underlying retinal pigment epithelium across all four quadrants. This comprehensive guide details the pathophysiology, surgical imperatives, and prognostic factors essential for the vitreoretinal specialist.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Indirect Ophthalmoscopy with scleral indentation (map breaks).
Step 2: B-Scan Ultrasonography (crucial if media is opaque/cataractous).
Step 3: OCT Macula to evaluate subretinal fluid and macular status.
Step 5: Systemic review (Blood pressure, blood sugar for PDR/Exudative causes).

rows: Fixed folds in all four quadrants

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: Membrane Peeling: Use ILM forceps to relieve tangential traction.
Retinotomy/Retinectomy: Mandatory for severe PVR (Grade C/D).
Tamponade Selection: C3F8 gas (long duration) vs. 1000/5000 cSt Silicone Oil.
Endolaser: Confluent barrage around all retinal breaks/tears.

content.explanation: F: Fundus exam; L: Lens/media clarity; U: Ultrasonography; I: Intraocular pressure; D: Demarcation lines/chronic changes.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: In TRD, always look for the 'unseen' break; peripheral breaks are often hidden by vitreous traction.
Silicone oil requires monitoring for secondary glaucoma and emulsification.
Macula-ON detachments should be operated within 24 hours to preserve 20/20 potential.
Always document the extent of retinal detachment in 'clock hours'.
